identity.name: Pico Trust
identity.value_proposition: Hide short trust signals inside ordinary images so they survive re-sharing.
identity.target_users: Journalists and fact-checkers who publish photos and need provenance to travel with them.

requirements.text: A user can embed a signed trust payload into an image.
requirements.acceptance: Given a PNG and a payload, when the user embeds it, then the returned image decodes back to the same payload.

requirements.text: A user can verify an image from the browser.
requirements.acceptance: Given an embedded image, when the user opens it in the web app, then the app shows the payload and whether it is intact.

overrides.reason: The api is a single-process prototype; structured logs are enough until it is deployed beyond one host.

decisions.title: Product identity
decisions.context: The project needed a name, audience and testable requirements before any code.
decisions.decision: Pico Trust targets journalists, with two acceptance-tested requirements.
decisions.consequences: Features outside R1 and R2 need a new requirement first.

decisions.title: Python api plus TypeScript web
decisions.context: Image processing is easiest in Python; verification needs a browser UI.
decisions.decision: A monorepo with an api (python) and a web (typescript) component.
decisions.consequences: Two toolchains to maintain; the api contract is the integration point.

decisions.title: User guide in docs/guide
decisions.context: Users need a guide to the web app and the public API.
decisions.decision: External docs live in docs/guide; api routes and web pages map to it.
decisions.consequences: A change to a route or page must update the guide.

decisions.title: GitHub Actions, container api, static web
decisions.context: Both components are deployed to staging and production.
decisions.decision: CI on GitHub Actions; api as a container on Fly.io, web on Cloudflare Pages.
decisions.consequences: Every push runs both components' checks; hosting is documented, not provisioned.

decisions.title: Conventional commits on trunk
decisions.context: A solo maintainer with agents committing needs a predictable history.
decisions.decision: Conventional commits scoped by component, committed straight to trunk.
decisions.consequences: The commit-msg hook rejects messages that break the convention.

decisions.title: Batched review
decisions.context: Reviewing every task is slow; unreviewed large diffs are risky.
decisions.decision: Batched review with a 200 line / 5 file threshold.
decisions.consequences: Agents stop for review once a batch crosses either limit.
